issue_context.title: Shelly devices not reconnecting after router reboot
issue_context.body:
## The problem
Using the new Shelly integration, devices are listed as  unavailable after the WifI router is restarted.

My router gets restarted each night and the Shelly devices are not reconnected. Only an HA restart resolves the issue.

The Shelly devices are fully accessible via ther IP addresses after the router reboot. No other network anomalies are occuring.

## Environment

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.115.5
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.13
- Integration causing this issue: shelly
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
Standard config flow implementation

## Traceback/Error logs
No log entries.

## Additional information
comments:
Fully reproducible. Consistently fails.
The only log entry is: 

```
2020-10-01 08:14:04 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.shelly] Timeout fetching Porch Lights data
2020-10-01 08:14:07 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.shelly] Timeout fetching Dining Light data
2020-10-01 08:14:07 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.shelly] Timeout fetching Shed data
```

Hey there @balloob, @bieniu, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`shelly`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L383) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I have the same issue. With a wall switch, I remove power from my Shelly bulbs. When enabling again, HA doesn't reconnect. I implemented a local fix for this, I'll push changes and see if it's an acceptable solution.

review_comments:
This invalidates every reference to blocks that entities hold. This is not good.

Instead we should see what connnection needs to be reinitialized and either set up aiocoap for automatic reconnect or set up aioshelly to be able to reconnect.
I see what you mean. Thanks for the hints, I'll give it another try.

@balloob Could you help me here a bit? It seems to be UDP6 which fails. Looking at the aiocoap, this is using sockets. The socket is still alive because the server side doesn't call close because it goes down hard. What I see happening (when removing the timeout on update in HA) is that aiocoap is programmed to make 4 retries and then it gets a timeout, but it's not really detected that the connection is broken (the socket send doesn't throw an error).

For aioshelly I can imagine a solution which would put a timeout on `coap_request` and recreates the `coap_context` when timeout happens. It wouldn't invalidate blocks, but is that an acceptable solution?
What do you think about changing coap message type? Look here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/40411#issuecomment-702324963
@bieniu Seems to work..I'll follow up in that issue.
